text:
alex: hitting a nasty edge with the async python client + streaming + retry/backoff. when a streaming request times out and the auth token refresh kicks in, the client retries by re-sending the *already-consumed* body and we end up with duplicate side-effects on the server. :facepalm:
maria: yikes. do you have a minimal repro?
alex: yep. simplified:
```py
# async streaming helper
async for chunk in client.chat.stream(prompt, retry_policy=RetryConfig(max_attempts=3)):
    process(chunk)
```
If the first stream gets a 502 after ~30s and our token refresh happens mid-stream, the library calls the retry path which attempts to reawait the same generator object. that fails to rewind and the server receives a truncated/duplicate payload.
devin: is this specific to streaming endpoints? or all POSTs with unseekable bodies?
alex: mostly streaming but also affects file-upload style flows where body is an async iterator. non-idempotent endpoints are being replayed without an idempotency header.
tyler: reproduce steps?
alex: 1) start a streaming request that yields chunks for a long time 2) simulate transient 502 + client-side timeout 3) trigger auth refresh (short-lived token) 4) observe retry attempt which resends the same generator -> server logs show duplicate processing id.
simon: does the client attach an idempotency token currently? I thought our default was to add one for non-GETs.
alex: only for the sync client POSTs where a body is bytes. not for async iterators. bug: idempotency header generation happens before request creation; when body is a generator we skip header to avoid false sense of safety.
maria: two problems then: (1) we should never auto-replay non-seekable bodies without explicit opt-in, (2) we need better typing to make async iterator bodies obvious to callers. mypy complaining that stream endpoint is annotated as AsyncIterator[str] but the implementation yields bytes -> mismatch.
devin: workaround for now?
alex: quick patch: explicitly set `retry_policy=RetryConfig(replay_unseekable=False)` and add an application-level idempotency token header when the server supports it. or wrap generator to buffer small N bytes to make it replayable (not ideal).
tiicket: created a small sample app to demonstrate — link: https://stash.redwood/sample-repro-stream-replay (internal)
ci-bot: ticket INF-4219 created for async-stream-replay-edgecase with severity=medium.
maria: propose long-term fix: (a) mark async iterator bodies as non-replayable by default; (b) add explicit api to opt-in to safe replay by providing an idempotency token or a rewindable buffer; (c) unify typing so `client.chat.stream` returns AsyncIterator[bytes] and SDK docs show that clearly.
tyler: agree. also add telemetry for "retry-with-unseekable-body" so we can detect how often this happens in prod.
simon: I'll take owner on a small RFC for the retry semantics + typing changes. will draft and ping y'all.
alex: thanks — pushed a tiny repro test under devex/integration that fails on current main. attaching logs:
```
[2026-03-12T15:23:01Z] request_id=abc123 status=502
[2026-03-12T15:23:02Z] token_refresh start
[2026-03-12T15:23:03Z] retry attempt=2 body=generator<stream_gen>
[2026-03-12T15:23:03Z] server processed idempotency_header=none -> side_effect_created id=xyz
[2026-03-12T15:23:04Z] server processed second request -> side_effect_created id=xyz-dup
```
maria: perfect repro. thanks alex. RFC when ready, @simon please include proposed wording for SDK release notes so users know the breaking typing change.
devin: also add a small sample snippet in quickstart showing how to provide an idempotency token for async streams.
alex: will do. staging test looks good with the buffered wrapper. will open a PR for the telemetry + ticket link.
ci-bot: PR #6123 opened by alex -> draft: fix/async-replay-safety
